$comment: Per-project settings for the session protocol. EDIT THIS FILE, never the scripts in .claude/scripts/ — they are byte-identical across projects and checked against the template. Every key is optional; missing keys fall back to the defaults shown here. Keys starting with $ are comments.
$protocol_version: Which DOCUMENT SHAPE this project is on. 1 = the original (CURRENT_STATE injected whole, ledger items injected as truncated full text, last 5 handoff lines). 2 = the budgeted shape (CURRENT_STATE is app state only; the ledger injects a one-line-per-item manifest plus full text for the items the NEXT ACTION cites; one handoff entry per track, in I-PASS shape). Set to 2 ONLY after running migrate-docs-v2.py — the scripts read this to decide how to render, and flipping it without migrating the documents just renders unmigrated docs a different way.
$payload: The session-start injection budget and its delivery. target_chars is the whole assembled payload, not one document — the only cap that stays honest when mass moves between documents (PROTOCOL.md 'Why this exists' #7); 25000 matches the ceiling Claude Code puts on its own auto-loaded MEMORY.md. Delivery is a separate constraint: Claude Code caps ONE hook string at 10,000 chars, so the hook emits the payload as parts — one `--part N` entry each in settings.json (five shipped) — of at most part_chars apiece; the deliverable ceiling is entries × part_chars, and check-payload-budget.py reports both. manifest_title_chars is how much of an item's TITLE becomes its manifest line (ID, tag and date are always shown; the provenance parenthetical never is). max_gating_items is how many items PER NEXT ACTION SECTION get full text because that section cites them; gating_item_max_chars caps one expansion's injected text (the ledger keeps the item whole). With two or more tracks on v2 the hook delivers only the core and each session loads its own track with `session-start-context.py --track <name>` (page_chars = one page of that output), so the budget is PER TRACK. The budget is a GATE at /end (check-payload-budget.py --strict --ratchet). ceiling_chars is NOT set by hand: a project already over the budget gets one per track from `check-payload-budget.py --init-ceiling`, every smaller wrap lowers it, and it disappears once the payload is inside the budget — raising it is raising the budget, which is the user's decision and a DECISIONS.md entry.
$spine_heading: Case-insensitive text of the ROADMAP.md heading that opens the status spine table. The start hook injects everything from that heading to the next '## '.
$check_command: Shell command run at /end Step 0c BEFORE anything is committed (build freshness, contract drift, typecheck). Non-zero exit stops the wrap. Empty = skipped. Example: "pnpm check". A track can override it with its own check_command inside its tracks entry ("" = that track runs no check — a marketing kit or docs track that never touches the build); a track touching shared_paths runs the repo-wide one as well.
$audit_command: Shell command run at session start; mentioned only if it reports findings. Example: "pnpm audit --prod" or "cargo audit". Empty = skipped.
$push_policy: "ask" = never push without asking (default). "standing" = session-end pushes are pre-authorised so work can continue from another machine — record that authorisation in DECISIONS.md first. Force pushes always need per-instance confirmation regardless.
$protected_branches: Branches a session must never commit to, e.g. ["main"] in a fork where main is a read-only mirror of upstream. The start hook trips the branch guard on them exactly as it does for a worktree. Empty = only worktrees and claude/* branches are guarded.
$upstream_ref: A remote-tracking ref this branch is periodically brought up to date with, e.g. "upstream/main" in a fork. The start hook fetches that remote and reports how many commits the ref has that HEAD lacks — reported, never acted on at start (merge or rebase is a session decision at a quiet point, per the project's DECISIONS.md). The statusline shows `upstream +N`. Empty = off.
$secret_scan: Run .claude/scripts/scan-secrets.py at /end Step 0c. Content-based; .gitignore is only a blocklist.
$index_skip_prefixes: Project-relative path prefixes (POSIX) the codebase-index hook ignores, on top of the built-in ones (.claude/, node_modules/, dist/, build/, target/, .next/, __pycache__/). Put generated code here, e.g. "apps/desktop/src-tauri/gen/".
$index_skip_suffixes: Extra file suffixes the codebase-index hook ignores, on top of the built-in binaries and media (images, video, audio, archives, fonts, compiled output, databases). Example: [".csv", ".svg"].
$ledger: Rules for docs/SESSION_LEDGER.md. v2 has NO cap on an item — items stay whole, the manifest protects the injection and payload.gating_item_max_chars caps an expansion (item_max_chars is read only by v1 projects; a v2 project may delete the key). open_soft_max is the count above which /end routes or closes the two oldest stale items, as a rate rather than a sitting. stale_after_days is what counts as old. move_closed_after_days MOVES struck lines to docs/SESSION_LEDGER_CLOSED.md — never deletes them, because an ID cited in a commit subject or a handoff entry must stay resolvable forever.
$file_caps: /end Step 0d (check-file-caps.py) — line caps on the CODE files this session touched (since the last wrap) and a same-basename twin check for new files. soft = flagged and put on the ledger (default 500); hard = the wrap stops (default 800); extensions = what counts as code (defaults cover TS/JS, Kotlin, Rust, Python, Swift, Java, Go, CSS, HTML, Vue, Svelte); skip_prefixes = paths the caps ignore on top of index_skip_prefixes, e.g. design prototypes or vendored code; twin_exempt = names the project repeats BY DESIGN, so a new one is not flagged as a twin — a folder prefix ending in / ("docs/marketing/posts/"), a bare file name anywhere ("routes.js"), or a path pattern matched segment by segment ("apps/server/src/*/routes.js"). Only for a layout that repeats a name on purpose; desktop's and mobile's own format.ts is the twin the check exists for.
$tracks: Parallel tracks — two sessions working on two VERSIONS of the app (e.g. desktop and mobile) in the same checkout on the same branch. Empty = single track (ledger IDs are L-N, no ownership rules). With 2+ tracks: each session declares its track at start, mints IDs with its own prefix (D-1, M-1 — independent counters, so no collisions), edits only its own 'owns' paths plus shared_paths, and the stop hook tolerates the OTHER track's uncommitted files only inside that track's owns. Optional "aliases": other words your existing docs use for the track ("android", "phone") — accepted in →tags and used to match legacy handoff lines. Optional "check_command": this track's own /end check (see $check_command). Example: [{"name": "desktop", "prefix": "D", "owns": ["apps/desktop/", "packages/frontend/"]}, {"name": "mobile", "prefix": "M", "owns": ["platforms/android/"], "aliases": ["android", "phone"]}]
$shared_paths: Paths every track may edit (shared packages, the server, docs). A change here that another track must ACT on (rebuild, redeploy, run a migration) gets a ledger line tagged for exactly those tracks, by name; a change nobody must act on is a stamped fact in CURRENT_STATE's Shared block. Example: ["packages/core/", "apps/server/"]
$shared_owner: Who owns an open problem found on a shared path (a server advisory, a warning, a shared script's bug): one track name for all shared paths, or {"apps/server/": "desktop", "scripts/": "desktop"} by path. Empty = the track that will fix it. Never →all: on one project 40 of 122 open items were →all because shared paths had no owner, and each rode in every track's start payload. The /end gate stops a wrap that adds an →all item from the wrapping track.
$state: Multi-track v2 only. Everything in CURRENT_STATE outside the NEXT ACTION sections is loaded by every track; a bullet tagged `- →<track>` is loaded only by that track. shared_max_chars caps the UNTAGGED bullets; at /end, state-archive.py moves the oldest (by the newest date in each) to docs/CURRENT_STATE_ARCHIVE.md, never loaded, and the gate stops a wrap that leaves them over. Exempt (never counted or moved): sections whose heading says 'blocker', and the never_move sections — each track's status of record, whose per-track rows are tagged instead. Raising shared_max_chars is raising what every session pays: the user's decision.
